_comment: All lengths are in INCHES. Source: Sleeves & Openings Standards Manual. Edit family names/params to match your library.
_familiesComment: Office (MPI) families, Revit 2026, category Mechanical Equipment. A null *Param is detected from the loaded family (Width/Length/Diameter/Comments and common variants); set it explicitly if detection picks the wrong one. Verify in Setup > Map Families.

roundSleeve._sizeTogglesComment: This family has no diameter parameter: each size is a Yes/No parameter '<prefix> <size>' (Storm 4..12, Sanitary 4..12, Vent 4..12, Fire 3..10, Gas 3..10, Cold Water 2..12, Hot Water 3..4, Electrical 2..5, Condensate 3). The add-in ticks the one for the system + size and unticks the rest; a size the family lacks rounds UP to the next available. TO CONFIRM WITH OFFICE: DryerExhaust -> Vent? Bathtub -> Sanitary (or the Double Sleeve for Tub family)? Sizes are sleeve sizes, not pipe sizes?

clearances._linkedComment: Columns, beams and walls are also read from linked Revit models (the structural model is usually a link). linkedModelMatch = regex on the link name, empty = all links.

levelClassification._comment: Regex (case-insensitive) matched against level names, tried in the order ignore, bulkhead, roof, setback, cellar; first match wins; unmatched levels are apartment floors. JSON needs \b for a regex word boundary. Ignore = reference levels (top of steel / slab, parapet): never a floor, nothing is placed or propagated there. Override any level in Project Setup.

generalRules._comment: Confirmed at the start of Project Setup and before any work (manual p.2). A No blocks the add-in.
mustConfirm: I am working from the Owner's plan, not the Approved plan.
I checked and confirmed this file is the latest version.

fixtures._comment: Manual p.2 'Always verify': the add-in finds these fixtures in the model (family/type/category name matched case-insensitively) and checks the sleeves against them in Final Check. Lengths in inches.

legend._comment: Auto Run: tag meanings are read from the engineer's PDF (ABBREVIATIONS table, SYMBOLS list, schedules). officeFixed = tags the office always uses and PDFs do not define (only KX and TX). categories are tried in order against the definition text (regex, case-insensitive); the first match wins. system = gets an opening of that system; ignore = no opening; labelOnHost = no opening, but the tag is added to the label of the duct opening it sits on (ERV-FSD). A definition matching nothing is 'not a riser'.

dwgProfile._comment: Auto Run: how the engineer draws risers in the DWG. riserBlocks = regex on the block (or dynamic-block source) name drawn at a riser's centre; tagBlocks = regex on the tag bubble block; tagAttributes = bubble attributes joined into the riser name (TX + 1 = TX1, ERV + SA = ERV-SA); connectorLayers = regex on layers of the line from bubble to riser. Distances in inches. Defaults match 24 Skillman (Precision Engineering Group).

adopt._comment: Setup > Adopt Existing: stamps openings/sleeves that were placed by hand so Final Check, Riser Manager, Propagate and Schedule see them. All regexes are case-insensitive. System is decided in this order: 1. nameToSystem on the label (nameParams) and on the type name; 2. for checkbox-sized sleeves, the prefix of the toggle that is ON via togglePrefixToSystem; 3. the matcher's default system. Systems the manual sizes (Exhaust, GarbageChute, DryerExhaust, MotorizedDamper, Refrigeration, Electrical, Storm, AreaDrain, Condensate, Standpipe, Bathtub, Toilet, ERV) get size checks; any other name (Sanitary, Vent, ColdWater, HotWater, Gas...) is still checked for structure, wall edges, overlaps and riser continuity.
